newsitem.title: UK: Dollar firms as mark shrivels on European crosses.
newsitem.headline: Dollar firms as mark shrivels on European crosses.

text.p: The dollar ended the European session firmer, setting a fresh 33-month high against the ailing yen and rebounding against the mark as concerns faded that the German easing cycle might have hit a bottom, traders said.
Dollar/yen strength was fuelled by the mark/yen cross, which set a fresh 3 1/2 year high at 74.48 yen.

Against the mark, the dollar bounced back above 1.52 marks, helped by the mark's retreat on its European crosses. The German currency was hit after several comments from Bundesbank members helped temper a sudden bout of German rate gloom this week.
"The likely scenario into next week is for dollar/yen to continue..(its) advance and for dollar/mark to go through a period of stabilisation," said Peter von Maydell at UBS, London.

At 1443 GMT, the dollar traded at 1.5238/49 marks, compared to 1.5214/24 marks in late European trading on Thursday. Dollar/yen was at 113.34/44 yen, off an earlier high at 113.45 but up from 112.81/91 at the previous close here.

Mark/yen, the motor behind the dollar's acceleration against the Japanese unit, was at 74.39/40, up from 74.13/16. Continued demand from Japanese investors, searching for higher yield, has fuelled the mark's rise.

Analysts said another slicing of the German repo rate over the coming months could not be ruled out completely. Even if there is no cut, like in Japan, there is no sign of any rate rise on the horizon.

The Bundesbank's chief economist Otmar Issing and council member Ernst Welteke said there was no need to cut rates now but held out hopes that the central bank could consider a further easing of the repo rate in future. Earlier this week, a comment by Issing had quashed hopes for lower rates.
Another Bundesbanker, Olaf Sievert, said the mark's exchange rate had not fully corrected from 1994/1995 highs.
"The net result of all these comments is that the market has regained some confidence that a repo cut is not totally out of the question," said a senior trader at a German bank in London.
Dollar/mark now has to overcome resistance at 1.5260 marks to focus on the upside, while dollar/yen looked set to target the January 1994 high at 113.58 next, the trader said.
"In perspective, we see the dollar's pullback this week as just a temporary correction," said Adrian Schmidt, economist at Chase Investment Bank in London.
The mark dropped back below 1,000 lire and set a 5-month low versus the French franc at 3.3735 in European trading.
The pound bounced back above 2.44 marks, while sterling set a fresh 15-month high at $1.6020. The low-yielding Swiss franc, meanwhile, fell to a 14-month low against the mark at 82.91.
The South African rand dropped to a record low. Dealers said speculative dollar demand out of London drove the rand to a low of 4.6150. Its previous record low was 4.5900, set on August 19.

The move was aggravated by comments from Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals who said credit might have to be tightened if there was no sign of a slowdown in bank credit extension and money supply growth. He saw no immediate need to increase rates at this stage though.

The Mexican peso was also hit amid sales by foreign investors and speculation about the renewal of the "pacto", an agreement on economic measures signed by the government, business and labour leaders which is hammered out and signed annually.
An unexpectedly high U.S. durable goods figure for September, showing a rise of 4.6 percent against 2.0 percent expected, was seen as dollar-supportive but had scant impact on trade.
